Team —

Attaching the SKU mapping worksheet and the current product-page draft we plan to push to the AWS listing this week. Acme asked for tighter regional examples and clearer wording around AMI/entitlement so their procurement team can sign off. High level asks from Acme:

- Show explicit regional examples (us-east-1 / eu-west-1) for how usage is metered.
- Clarify AMI naming and which AMI is included in the private offer.
- Make the "Billing & Pricing" section show a concrete example (monthly bill for 100k tokens + reserved throughput) rather than abstract text.

What I need from you: quick pass on copy and SKU sheet by 12:00 PT today so we can send to Acme before their internal procurement meeting tomorrow. Priorities: accuracy for AMI & entitlement rows in the worksheet, and one concise paragraph for the product page that explains the co-sell benefits (what they get from Redwood + how marketplace billing appears).

Attachments: sku-mapping.xlsx (worksheet with regional rows), product-page-draft.md (current copy), ami-naming-guidelines.pdf (vendor-standard naming).

Suggested process:
- Jonas: review SKU mapping AMI/entitlement rows (tab: "Entitlement")
- Ben: quick legal-safe wording for the billing example (tab: "Pricing Examples")
- Marissa: UX copy edit + co-sell paragraph

I'll consolidate changes and reply back to Acme with an updated draft.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for sending. A few clarifications from our side after an internal read:

1) Regional billing example: please show a two-region example (us-east-1 + eu-west-1) where a customer uses 60% of tokens from us-east and 40% from eu-west. We need to confirm the marketplace metering behavior across regions for our finance team.

2) AMI naming: our security team needs the AMI label to include the image hash and the published timestamp. Your ami-naming-guidelines.pdf is helpful; can the product page state "AMI: redwood-inference/v1.4.2 (sha256:abcd...) published 2027-03-22" as the exemplar? We need exactness.

3) PrivateOffer entitlements: we requested a single SKU for "Dedicated Inference - small pool" and a separate SKU for "Burst capacity add-on". In the spreadsheet the small-pool and burst rows look merged — can you split them and call out the fallback policy in the product page?

4) Co-sell paragraph: our GTM lead asked for one sentence that highlights joint support (e.g., "co-managed onboarding with Acme and Redwood"), and one sentence about the benefits to the end user (reduced latency from regional routing, single bill via AWS Marketplace).

We appreciate the quick turnaround. If you send an updated draft by 2pm PT we can move to procurement review.

Best,
Elena Torres
Head of Cloud Partnerships | Acme Analytics
elena.torres@acme-analytics.com
